children: The U.S. corn crop was in 57% good/excellent condition this week, up from 56% the week before but down from 67% this time last year, according to the USDA's latest report. The corn harvest was 8% complete compared with 7% a year ago. "The widespread heatwaves seen to finish the growing season have certainly sped up maturity, but scattered heavy rains across the Midwest in the last week ultimately kept somewhat of a lid on progress at the national level," Mike Castle of StoneX says in a note. Soybeans were 58% good/excellent, with 6% harvested. That's double the five-year average of 3%, "again reflecting the rapid maturation due to recent excessive heat," Castle adds. The spring wheat harvest is 93% complete, with winter wheat 8% planted. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
